transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-07
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Sofia Ruiz (CTO - Lark), Mark Bennett (Lead ML Eng - Lark), Priya Kaur (Infra - Lark), Aaron Li (Product - Lark)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — i'm maya, i'm the account lead on this. ethan is our se who will drive the technical bits. can we do quick intros from the lark side?
[00:10] Sofia: yeah hi i'm sofia, cto at lark, we own the roadmap for search and question-answering.
[00:16] Mark: mark here, lead ml eng, i'll run the benchmark and coordinate infra.
[00:20] Priya: priya, infra, focused on VPC, networking and security constraints.
[00:25] Aaron: aaron on product.
[00:27] Ethan: cool — high level for today's call: we want to align on success criteria for the POC, define latency/throughput SLOs, pick measurement definitions (we'll talk TTFT vs TPOT), size the workload and agree on a benchmark plan and timeline.

[00:45] Sofia: the main ask from our side is interactive speed for our in-app assistant. we need snappy responses — ideally users shouldn't feel lag. so p95 is our main focus, p99 is also important for spikes.
[00:58] Mark: to add, our current infra has about 120 qps at peak across similar features, but average is 20 qps. token lengths vary — typical prompt ~80 tokens, response ~120 tokens, but we have longer flows up to 512 tokens in tests.

[01:20] Ethan: got it. important to define the metrics. quick definitions so everyone's aligned: TTFT — time to first token, measures initial latency to start of generation; TPOT — time to produce tokens (end-to-end for whole output), which captures tail behavior for long responses.
[01:36] Maya: yeah, we've seen customers focus on TTFT for perceived latency and TPOT for throughput/cost analysis.

[01:45] Priya: which should we optimize for here? our UX indicates users notice initial lag more than token drip.
[01:52] Aaron: agree, but some flows need complete answer quickly (like short answers), so TPOT for p99 matters for reliability.

[02:05] Ethan: recommendation: define two primary SLOs for the POC: TTFT p95 <= 300ms, TTFT p99 <= 650ms for short responses (<=128 tokens). And TPOT p95 <= 800ms, TPOT p99 <= 1.5s for mid-length responses (<=256 tokens). these numbers are initial proposals — flexible based on sample traces.
[02:28] Mark: that p95 300ms is aggressive but not impossible if model and infra are right; are these numbers for hosted or dedicated?
[02:36] Maya: good q — these are achievable on Dedicated capacity with low-batch settings and optimized kernels; hosted may hit them for smaller batch sizes but depends on model variant and region. we'll include both hosted and dedicated configs in the plan.

[02:50] Sofia: what about model variants and quantization? we plan to test both a base open model and a trimmed/quantized variant.
[02:58] Ethan: we'll test multiple variants. our typical POC matrix: model A (fp16), model A quantized (int8/4), and a smaller faster model for failover. We'll measure TTFT and TPOT across the matrix and include kv/prefix cache scenarios.

[03:15] Priya: network hops matter. we will likely run Lark infra in GCP us-central, we need Redwood to run benchmarks in same region to avoid cross-region noise.
[03:24] Ethan: yes we'll use a Redwood sandbox in us-central, and can also run tests in your VPC if you prefer. for initial bench we'll do same-region to isolate model/runtime behavior.

[03:36] Aaron: workload sizing — mark said peaks ~120 qps. what's a realistic test load?
[03:42] Ethan: propose tests at 1 qps, 20 qps (avg), 80 qps (sustained), and 150 qps (peak spike). we'll run steady-state for 10-15 minutes per point and collect p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and TPOT, plus CPU/GPU utilization, batch sizes, and KV cache hit rate.

[04:05] Mark: can we emulate our token distribution? we have a long-tail — most are short but 5% above 256 tokens. we'll share a histogram.
[04:13] Maya: please do. mark, action item to export prompt samples and a token histogram.

[04:20] Mark: yep will do.

[04:22] Ethan: measurement plan specifics: sampling frequency — we'll collect per-request telemetry at 100% for the test windows. for longer production runs we sample 5-10%. TTL for logs we'll keep locally for the POC. instrumented metrics: request_id, model_variant, seq_in, seq_out, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, TTFT_ms, TPOT_ms, batch_size, cache_hit boolean.
[04:48] Priya: is request-level logging safe for us? we need redaction options and no PII in logs.
[04:54] Maya: yes Redwood supports masking and optional prompt redaction in logs; we will provide privacy configs and a SOC2 summary.

[05:04] Ethan: about measurement definitions, a couple of gotchas: TTFT needs to be measured from request ingress to generation of first token emitted by the runtime, not when the first byte of the response reaches client, to avoid client-side network variability. TPOT is measured from ingress to last token emitted. we'll include both server-side and end-to-end (client) latency in the report.

[05:26] Aaron: how do you handle batching impact? a larger batch improves throughput but increases TTFT for some requests.
[05:32] Ethan: exactly — we'll run both single-request (batch size=1) and auto-batched runs. We'll capture distribution of batch sizes during the run. For SLO decisions, many customers pick conservative settings: configure lower max-batch (e.g., 4) and aggressive batching timeouts to balance latency vs cost. We'll surface cost delta in the benchmark report.

[05:55] Sofia: can we see historical benchmarks? like similar customers?
[06:00] Maya: we'll share anonymized bench summaries and a template spreadsheet that maps qps + model -> expected p95/p99 for TTFT/TPOT.

[06:08] Mark: about success criteria — beyond meeting p95/p99 numbers, we want reproducibility in our infra and a clear path to production (Dedicated).
[06:15] Maya: agreed. recommend success criteria list: 1) Achieve TTFT and TPOT targets for the representative workload in same-region tests; 2) Demonstrate stable resource utilization (GPU < 80% on average for target qps); 3) Run 1-hour sustained test at 80 qps without error spike; 4) Walkthrough of rollout plan for Dedicated and security signoffs.
[06:40] Ethan: timeline proposal: share bench plan and scripts by 9/9, lark provides prompt set by 9/10, perf run week of 9/14, 1-2 day analysis/report by 9/18, follow-up demo of results 9/20.
[06:55] Sofia: that timeline works for us.

[07:00] Priya: network requirements — we'll need an allowlist for Redwood IPs if we run within our VPC; also we'll want to test with KMS integrated for key management.
[07:09] Maya: we'll include IP ranges and a KMS integration checklist in the security docs.

[07:16] Aaron: quick qu on cost modeling: will Redwood provide sample cost per 1M tokens for Hosted vs Dedicated baseline?
[07:22] Maya: yes we'll include initial pricing estimate in the follow-up. Dedicated pricing will be modeled on expected GPU utilization from the bench.

[07:30] Mark: any hidden caveats measuring p99? sampling noise at low qps can make p99 unstable.
[07:36] Ethan: good point — we'll ensure enough samples by extending the duration at lower qps or aggregating multiple windows. also compute confidence intervals for percentiles.

[07:46] Sofia: ok next steps recap?
[07:48] Maya: recap: maya to send benchmark plan + scripts by 9/9; redwood to attach security docs by 9/8; mark to share prompt set and histograms by 9/10; schedule perf run week of 9/14; ethan to prepare test configs for TTFT/TPOT.

[08:05] Mark: noted.

[08:07] Maya: anything else?

[08:09] Priya: just confirm region — us-central.
[08:11] Ethan: confirmed.
[08:12] Maya: cool thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the plan and calendar invites.
[08:16] Sofia: thanks all.

End of meeting.

Notes/Observations: transcript includes some automatic transcription errors in a few proper nouns, but technical content and objective alignment are clear. The team is focused on p95 perceived latency and p99 tail behavior, will run same-region benchmarks across model variants and caching scenarios, and has an agreed timeline for the POC perf run and deliverables.
